extracted.intended_audience: QHP issuers, State Exchanges, web-brokers/agents/brokers, State and Federal regulators, and other health insurance stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and compliance standards for the CMS proposed Payment Notice and Exchange rule (CMS-9883-P), including ECP/NA data collection, HHS-RADV, risk adjustment user fee, state exchange operations, SBE-EDE, QIS, rate filing justification, and consumer consent documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECP requirements for non-network plans (proposed §156.236(b)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans must demonstrate they meet ECP related requirements at §156.236(b)(1) through (3) such as: whether the non-network plan meets at least a minimum percentage, as specified by HHS, of available ECPs that accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full in each plan's service area collectively across all ECP categories defined under §156.235(a)(2)(ii)(B), and at least a minimum percentage of available ECPs in each plan's service area within certain individual ECP categories, as specified by HHS; whether the non-network plan offers the benefit amount as payment in full to at least one ECP in each of the eight ECP categories per county in the plan's service area described in §156.235(a)(2)(ii)(B); and whether the non-network plan offers the benefit amount as payment in full to all available Indian health care providers in the plan's service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These substantive thresholds (minimum percentages across categories, at least one ECP per category per county, and coverage of all available Indian health care providers) are the metrics non-network plans must satisfy to demonstrate compliance with the proposed ECP requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of ECP data in MPMS for non-network plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans must submit ECP data in MPMS to demonstrate they meet proposed ECP requirements, using MPMS to select prepopulated eligible ECPs and to select modified statuses describing whether a select ECP was offered or accepted their benefit amount as payment in full (rather than contract statuses used by network plans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPMS UI displays qualified and eligible ECPs in the issuer's State and is regularly updated (removes closed/ineligible ECPs). This is intended to reduce issuer burden versus manually inputting facility details. Non-network plans will use MPMS selection of ECPs and modified 'offered/accepted payment-in-full' statuses to satisfy §156.236(b)(1)-(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation question burden estimate (PRA burden estimate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated time for responding to the attestation questions for a single non-network plan ranges between thirty seconds to one minute for each of the six attestation questions, likely requiring a maximum of six minutes total to complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS expects the extra time and costs associated with completing this section would be negligible to flat, and that many current ECP/NA collection requirements already apply and will be streamlined via MPMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Improvement Strategy (QIS) data collection status and submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no information collection associated with this proposed policy change to QIS and no changes are proposed to the QIS data collection requirements applicable to QHP issuers (QIS data collection is approved under OMB Control Number 0938-1286). Elsewhere in the proposal, HHS proposes modifying requirements to require QHP issuers to submit any two of five quality improvement strategies (QISs) topic areas listed in section 1311(g)(1) of the Affordable Care Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule clarifies there is no new ICR for QIS data collection in this action, but proposes a substantive change to require submission of two of five QIS topic areas — stakeholders should note both the existing ICR approval and the substantive submission requirement proposal and comment as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA-related public comment submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting PRA-related comments, commenters must identify the rule [CMS-9883-P], the ICR's CFR citation, CMS ID number, and OMB control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS has submitted the proposed rule to OMB for review of information collection requirements; the ICRs are not effective until OMB approval. To obtain supporting statements/forms, visit CMS' PRA webpage or call the Reports Clearance Office. ICR-related comments must be submitted by the ICR comment due date and include the specified identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Analysis and accounting statement per OMB Circular A-4
rubrics_metrics.description: A Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) was prepared in keeping with Executive Order 12866, and an accounting statement (Table 20) showing the classification of the impacts associated with provisions of the proposed rule was prepared as required by OMB Circular A-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Orders and OMB guidance direct agencies to assess costs and benefits and, where appropriate, present monetized and qualitative impacts. The preamble notes OIRA has determined the rulemaking is 'significant' under EO12866 section 3(f). Stakeholders may comment on the RIA's assumptions and estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS-RADV error estimation modification to incorporate IVA sampling changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed addition of an additional scaling factor to the HHS-RADV error estimation methodology to ensure that HCC-associated error rates apply only to the proportion of total PLRSs associated with HCC components of EDGE risk scores; the factor captures the proportion of an issuer's population risk arising from enrollees with HCCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simulations showed HHS-RADV adjustments decreased in magnitude with the additional scaling factor. HHS solicits comments on the estimated impacts of this proposal; the change is intended to more accurately assess risk attributable to enrollees with HCCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS risk adjustment user fee methodology and proposed rate (§153.610(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2027 benefit year, HHS proposes to use the same methodology as the 2026 Payment Notice to estimate administrative expenses for operating HHS risk adjustment and proposes a risk adjustment user fee of $0.20 PMPM for 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS expects user fee collections to be similar to prior estimates and seeks comment on these impact estimates and assumptions; the fee funds HHS' operation of risk adjustment on behalf of States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Rate Filing Justification URRT CSR reporting requirements (§154.215)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement for issuers to report, as part of the rate filing justification, URRT entries on adjustments to the index rate to account for unreimbursed CSRs: actual CSR amounts paid on behalf of eligible enrollees, additional revenue collected from previous applied CSR load (using standard methodology in §156.430(c)(2)), amount previously generated by any load factors, projected CSR amounts expected to be paid in the upcoming plan year, additional revenue to be collected due to the CSR load factor, CSR load factors in a new dedicated line item, and the expected amount generated by the load factor for the upcoming plan year. Issuers must also explain in the Actuarial Memorandum the methodology used to determine the load factor and how the expected amount generated compares to expected CSR payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS estimates significant one-time and ongoing implementation costs for issuers and some federal review costs; the enhanced CSR reporting aims to improve accuracy and transparency in CSR load setting and may affect premiums and PTC calculations. HHS seeks comments on costs, impacts, and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of State Exchange — removal of SBE-FP prerequisite (§155.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove §155.105(b)(4) rescinding the 2025 Payment Notice requirement that a State must first operate for at least one plan year an SBE-FP before operating a State Exchange. Instead, a State must demonstrate its ability to operationalize State Exchange functional requirements through HHS' review process; whether a State first operates an SBE-FP does not change the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS believes rescinding the SBE-FP prerequisite returns flexibility to States and does not impose new requirements; States still must undergo the established review/approval process to demonstrate readiness to operate a State Exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval documentation for State Exchange establishment (§155.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to amend §155.106(a)(2) to rescind the 2025 Payment Notice requirement that a State must provide supporting documentation demonstrating progress toward meeting or implementing State Exchange Blueprint requirements as part of establishment activities; HHS may still request supplemental documentation under the Blueprint approval process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed change does not impose new requirements; States should expect that HHS may request supporting documentation as part of normal review and approval activities for a State Exchange Blueprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange centralized eligibility and enrollment system requirement (§155.205(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §155.205(b) to specify a State Exchange is not limited to operating a centralized eligibility and enrollment consumer interface on the Exchange website as the only model for supporting consumer application submission and QHP enrollment; however, the State Exchange must make all determinations of eligibility for QHP coverage and insurance affordability programs and maintain records of all QHP enrollments, and must maintain a centralized eligibility and enrollment system and a website providing standardized comparative information on plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Exchanges may delegate consumer-facing enrollment functionality to non-Exchange entities (web-brokers, direct enrollment entities) that demonstrate operational readiness and compliance via robust approval/oversight per §155.221(j), but the Exchange remains responsible for eligibility determinations, records, and standardized plan information.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBE-Enhanced Direct Enrollment option approval and State responsibilities (§155.221(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to add §155.221(k) establishing an SBE-Enhanced Direct Enrollment (SBE-EDE) option allowing State Exchanges, subject to HHS approval, to leverage direct enrollment technology and rely primarily on private-sector enrollment pathways operated by issuers, web-brokers, and agents/brokers. States electing SBE-EDE must revise their Exchange Blueprint to describe implementation, meet required minimum Exchange functions, implement interfaces to approved EDE entities, and maintain oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation impacts depend on number of States electing SBE-EDE. States may incur start-up/interface costs but may save on consumer-facing website costs. States remain responsible for approval, oversight, and ensuring EDE entities meet security, privacy, operational, EDN, and data requirements; HHS oversight costs expected to be nominal given existing mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: EDE entity technical, security, and operational requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective EDE entities must implement nearly 300 security and privacy controls consistent with CMS' system security and privacy plan, contract with independent third-party auditors for security/privacy assessment test plans, submit quarterly Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), contract for annual independent assessments consistent with continuous monitoring requirements, and implement dynamic UIs, post-enrollment support functionality, and interfaces to provide all information necessary for eligibility determinations (APTC, CSR, Medicaid, CHIP) and to display eligibility determination notices (EDNs) to consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These technical and compliance controls are prerequisites for approval; EDE entities must show privacy/security posture via audits and ongoing reporting. Consumers completing applications on EDE sites must receive EDNs and the same eligibility information as if they used the State Exchange site. States can partner with Federal EDE partners to achieve savings; EDE entity costs may be offset by fee arrangements among market participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of State-required benefits as 'in addition to EHB' (proposed §155.170(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to amend §155.170(a)(2) so that any State-required benefits are considered 'in addition to EHB' (and thus not EHB) if they meet four conjunctive elements: (1) required by a State action taking place after December 31, 2011; (2) applicable to the small group and/or individual markets; (3) specific to required care, treatment, or services; and (4) not required by State action for purposes of compliance with Federal requirements. Effective beginning with PY 2027 under the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this classification, such State-required benefits would require defrayal by the State; States should evaluate overlaps between mandates and EHB benchmark plans. The proposal may change whether certain State actions trigger defrayal obligations; HHS solicits comments on administrative/defrayal cost estimates and on the proposed effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of HHS-approved consumer consent form for eligibility application review (§155.220(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments to §§155.220(j)(2)(ii)(A) and (j)(2)(iii)(A) to require agents, brokers, and web-brokers to use the HHS-approved and -created consumer consent form to meet eligibility application review requirements and consent documentation requirements, eliminating current broad allowances for meeting these requirements and clarifying what actions constitute 'taking an action' to meet regulatory obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HHS-approved form creates an objective standard to reduce confusion and protect consumers and improves HHS' ability to investigate potentially noncompliant agents/brokers/web-brokers. Entities that previously relied exclusively on phone recordings, text messages, or other non-HHS-approved methods would be affected; consumers interacting by phone may perceive the new requirement as burdensome, but it ensures required information is documented and streamlines compliance review.
